source.title: Cortical and subcortical contributions to Stop signal response inhibition: role of the subthalamic nucleus

confidence_rationale: Canonical foundation for the reactive/STN half: right IFC and STN are specifically activated by stopping (not going), and stopping-related activation is greater for FAST inhibitors than slow ones in both regions, with IFC and STN activity correlated -- convergent, independent support that the fast reactive route runs through the STN and that its engagement tracks stopping speed. Lower confidence (0.62) because it is a 2006 activation/correlation study that only hypothesises the hyperdirect projection (its closing sentence calls for future work to establish a direct IFC-STN pathway), speaks only to the reactive half, and says nothing about proactive control or non-collapsibility.
failure_signatures: The paper itself does not demonstrate the hyperdirect pathway -- it explicitly leaves establishing a direct IFC->STN projection to future research; it shows co-activation and correlation, not connectivity.

It addresses only reactive stopping; it provides no evidence for a separate proactive pathway or for the two operating at segregated, non-collapsible timescales, so it cannot on its own distinguish MECH-141 from a single-pathway account.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a stop-signal fMRI task, right inferior frontal cortex (IFC) and the subthalamic nucleus (STN) are activated by stopping; stopping-related activation is greater in fast than slow inhibitors in both regions and is correlated across subjects, suggesting the STN suppresses thalamocortical output to block response execution -- possibly via a hyperdirect IFC-STN projection (left for future work).
mapping.ree_translation: Independent, canonical corroboration of MECH-141's fast reactive pathway: the STN is the subcortical node that halts an initiated action, and the degree of IFC/STN engagement tracks how fast the stop is -- consistent with a fast interrupt route whose recruitment sets abort latency.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is co-activation and individual-difference correlation, not a demonstrated pathway or a latency measurement, and it covers only the reactive half. Its role in the pull is convergent foundational support for the fast route, superseded on the connectivity/timing specifics by Chen 2020 and Jahfari 2011.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI (two experiments, incl. high-resolution structural/functional confirmation of STN-vicinity activation), stop-signal task, healthy adults.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (J Neurosci, foundational, heavily replicated). Mapping fidelity modest: co-activation/correlation only, reactive half only, hyperdirect projection hypothesised not shown. Transfer risk low-moderate (healthy human fMRI). Included as the independent canonical anchor for the fast route; the newer papers in this pull carry the connectivity and timing specifics.
